newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Nobel peace laureate said too busy to meet Kohl.
newsitem.headline: Nobel peace laureate said too busy to meet Kohl.

text.p: Nobel peace laureate Bishop Carlos Belo apparently refused an invitation to meet German Chancellor Helmut Kohl during his official visit to Indonesia, officials said on Monday.
Kohl told a news conference the German side had sought a month ago through the Vatican and the church in Indonesia to invite the East Timorese bishop to a meeting in Jakarta.
"I regret it was cancelled," Kohl said, adding that apparently Belo was busy touring East Timor.

Kohl arrived in Jakarta on Saturday for his fourth visit to Indonesia since 1983. He spent a relaxed day fishing in the Java Sea with Indonesian President Suharto on Sunday before the official leg of his visit on Monday.
German delegation sources said Kohl had been expected to meet Belo, but the bishop failed to appear at a meeting the chancellor had on Monday afternoon with other Indonesian church leaders.
There was no response from phone calls to Belo's home in the East Timor capital, Dili, or from church aides in the former Portuguese colony.
Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas told a news briefing Belo might have had previous commitments.
"I heard that Bishop Belo had some other commitments and unfortunately that (meeting) has not taken place yet. Maybe it will take place before he (Kohl) leaves but I don't know."

Belo was jointly awarded the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize early this month together with self-exiled East Timorese resistance leader Jose Ramos-Horta, who had called on Kohl to raise the East Timor issue with Suharto.
Indonesian troops took over East Timor in December 1975 and Jakarta declared it Indonesia's 27th province the following July in a move the United Nations has refused to recognise.

Officials said human rights, East Timor and trade and economic cooperation were among the topics in 90 minutes of official talks between Kohl and Suharto at the state Merdeka (Freedom) Palace in central Jakarta.
Kohl also had an hour-long closed-door meeting with Cardinal Julius Darmaatmadja, the head of the Bishops' Conference of Indonesia, and the Catholic bishops of Bogor and Medan.
Issues discussed included East Timor and the burning of churches by a Moslem mob in East Java earlier this month, Darmaatmadja said.

"On the part of Bishops Conference, we said that the inter-religious relations cases which had flared up recently were not in itself religious problems, but more...like problems of social injustice," he told reporters after the meeting. "So there should not be any interpretation that it was a problem between religions."
